reason: The complete batch review found three locally repairable prerequisite/proof gaps. The open problem keeps the recent claimed solution qualified as unverified; no Statement or Definition rewrite is requested, so no consumer dispositions are required.

findings.reason: The Definition says the local well-posedness lemma supplies existence, uniqueness, representative independence, and boundedness, but does not record that well-definedness result in justified_by. The lemma already depends on this Definition, so it can be recorded as justified_by rather than deps, without a cycle.

The Statement asserts a bounded bilinear form, while the proof establishes existence, uniqueness, representative independence, and the bound but does not explicitly prove bilinearity. Add the short uniqueness argument showing linearity of the weak solution in the first datum and of the pairing in the second.

Steps 1.3 and 2.1 use the classical chain rule for H1 functions. Step 1.2 establishes bounded composition by density but does not explicitly extend the weak-gradient formula and energy change-of-variables identity to H1 classes. Add that passage using smooth approximation, bounded derivatives, and change of variables.

The 2018 survey describes general smooth anisotropic uniqueness with full or local data as open ([Daudé–Kamran–Nicoleau §1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.00910)); the item also cites a 2026 [primary-hosted preprint](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf) claiming the same-patch result. I could not retrieve and read that proof, so I did not validate it. The item already marks the claim unverified and does not use it as a supplier.
